subject: Request: approval for early-exit transition credit and opt-out language (BrightWave)
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Request: approval for early-exit transition credit and opt-out language (BrightWave)

Team —

BrightWave is pushing for a flexible early-exit option in the enterprise expansion we're closing next week. They want a formal opt-out clause that allows them to downsize at 30/60/90 day milestones during year 1 with a corresponding transition credit. They've asked for the credit to be applied as a percentage of committed monthly spend dependent on when they opt out (they proposed 60% at 30 days, 30% at 60 days, 0% at 90 days).

Key asks from the customer:
- Formal opt-out calendar (30/60/90)
- Transition credit schedule tied to remaining committed spend
- Clear language that Redwood can reassign dedicated capacity after the opt-out window

Why this matters: BrightWave is a strategic healthcare customer (HIPAA scope to follow), but this concession materially affects revenue recognition and capacity planning for the Dedicated pool. We can accept a staged transition credit if leadership approves a 12-week ramp protection for Redwood (i.e., we reserve the right to charge a minimum ramp amount for the first 12 weeks post-commit).

I've attached the SOW with the customer's proposed redlines and my suggested language (redlines_early-exit.docx). Asking for:
- Marcus/Monica: recommend approval or alternatives to the percentages above
- Markus: executive sign-off if you agree with the 12-week ramp protection + the proposed 30/60/90 credit schedule

If approved, Legal will turn this into final contract language and Sales Ops will update billing triggers.

Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: SOW_BrightWave_v2.pdf (SOW draft), redlines_early-exit.docx (proposed clause)
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 10:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: approval for early-exit transition credit and opt-out language (BrightWave)

Vanessa —

Thanks for the write-up and the redlines. My take: the customer-proposed credits are aggressive but not unreasonable given the size of the expansion and their procurement calendar. I propose we counter with the following:
- 30 days: 50% transition credit
- 60 days: 25% transition credit
- 90 days: 0%
- A 12-week minimum ramp protection fee equal to 40% of committed monthly spend if they downsize during that window (to cover redeployment & capacity loss)

Rationale: keeps the customer comfortable while protecting our near-term unit economics. If Leadership signs off, we should require a signed mutual action plan (MAP) with the opt-out dates and an explicit clause allowing Redwood to reassign Dedicated capacity after 12 weeks.

Also, cc'ing Finance for a quick check on revenue recognition mechanics — we need to ensure we can amortize any credits as a deduction to deferred revenue rather than an on-invoice discount.

Marcus
Director, Strategic Sales

Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 13:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: approval for early-exit transition credit and opt-out language (BrightWave)

Thanks, Vanessa and Marcus —

Appreciate the quick response and proposal. From BrightWave's side we want predictability for our budget and the flexibility to scale down if clinical priorities shift. A few clarifying points:
- The credit percentages Marcus suggested are reasonable; we'd like confirmation on whether credits are one-time adjustments or applied across remaining invoices.
- We need the opt-out to be exercisable at the month boundary (i.e., notice by the 15th for next-month adjustment) rather than a rolling day count.
- Can Redwood include language that any reassignment of capacity will be communicated 30 days in advance and will not affect current integrations?

If you can provide revised contract language that spells out timing and how credits are applied, we can loop in procurement and legal on our side.

Sara Liu
VP, Digital Health Programs
BrightWave Health

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 16:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: approval for early-exit transition credit and opt-out language (BrightWave)

Team —

After reviewing the SOW and the proposed counter, I'm prepared to approve the concession with conditions. Approve the following commercial framework for BrightWave:

1) Transition credit schedule (approved): 50% at 30 days, 25% at 60 days, 0% at 90 days. Credits will be applied as a one-time adjustment to deferred revenue tied to the remaining committed spend and will be documented as a billing credit in the first invoice following opt-out.

2) 12-week ramp protection (approved): Redwood will retain a ramp protection fee equal to 40% of the committed monthly spend for any downsize exercised within the first 12 weeks after expansion goes live. This fee covers redeployment and capacity reservation.

3) Notice & timing (approved): Opt-out must be submitted by the 15th of the month for the change to take effect the following calendar month. Redwood will notify BrightWave 30 days in advance of any capacity reassignment; reassignment language must include mitigations that prevent disruption to integrations during the 30-day notice period.

4) Legal & Finance: authorize Legal to convert the redlined language into final contract wording and Finance to confirm revenue recognition entries. Please loop in Legal (cc: aditya_rao@redwood.ai) and Sales Ops to prepare the final MAP and DocuSign packet.

Markus Klein
VP, Sales Operations (Interim)
Redwood Inference

Next steps: Vanessa, please send the updated redlines to BrightWave and share the final DocuSign link once Legal confirms the language. I'll approve the deviation and brief RevOps on the reporting impact once Finance confirms the amortization approach.

-Markus
